overall_summary: Bitcoin looks supported today by strong ETF inflows and whale accumulation, while the soft jobs report drove yields and the dollar lower and cut Fed hike odds. Geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and delayed U.S. crypto legislation add some caution, but the macro backdrop remains favorable for crypto. Traders will watch Wednesday's CPI for the next catalyst.
key_points: Whales buy over 1.2B BTC this week
Soft jobs cut Fed hike odds, yields drop
Middle East strikes and sanctions add risk
CLARITY Act vote delayed into September

items.title: BIP-110 Minority Fork Stalls After Just Two Blocks
items.summary: Supporters of the controversial BIP-110 soft fork, which aims to temporarily limit arbitrary data in Bitcoin transactions, split off at block 961632 but the enforcing chain produced only two blocks before grinding to a halt. With miner signaling stuck around two to three percent and the minority chain dozens of blocks behind due to full difficulty and tiny hashrate, it has no realistic path to lock-in. Traders should care because it removes a major near-term chain-split and replay-attack overhang, though residual confusion or wallet risks linger while the main chain powers ahead unimpeded.
items.impact: Reduces fork uncertainty, supportive for stability near 65k

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Pull 853 Million in Five-Day Inflow Streak
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately 853.5 million dollars in net inflows across five consecutive sessions from August 3 to 7, with BlackRock's IBIT taking the lion's share around 80 percent or nearly 700 million. August flows are already several times July's total and reverse prior outflows, while Ethereum ETFs added another 245 million. This is pure institutional demand that traders watch closely because it absorbs supply and has historically underpinned price floors even when spot action looks choppy around 65k.
items.impact: Strong buying pressure and institutional floor under BTC

items.title: MARA Pledges 18750 BTC as Collateral for 600 Million Loans
items.summary: Bitcoin miner MARA Holdings pledged 18,750 BTC worth roughly 1.2 billion dollars to secure 600 million in new Bitcoin-backed loans from Coinbase Credit and Two Prime, partly to fund its Long Ridge energy and AI infrastructure push. The collateral represents over half its reported holdings, and the facilities carry around 7.5 percent rates maturing in 2028. Traders care because large miners locking up rather than dumping BTC is constructive, yet it adds leverage and potential forced-sale risk if price drops sharply and triggers margin calls.
items.impact: Collateral use avoids immediate sell pressure but raises leverage risk

items.title: Whales Accumulate Over 1.2 Billion in Bitcoin This Week
items.summary: On-chain data shows wallets holding 10 to 10,000 BTC added more than 20,000 coins, roughly 1.2 billion dollars, since late July while price chopped below 65k. This stealth accumulation ran alongside the strong ETF inflows and occurred with little retail conviction. For traders it signals smart money building positions in the current range, often a precursor to larger moves once catalysts align, providing a potential support wall around recent levels.
items.impact: Builds on-chain support and reduces available supply

items.title: Senate Pushes CLARITY Act Vote into September
items.summary: U.S. Senate leadership delayed a floor vote on the landmark crypto market structure CLARITY Act until after the August recess, targeting a procedural window in mid-September. The bill had already faced tight timelines and limited Democratic support. Traders should note that prolonged regulatory uncertainty can cap upside and keep institutions cautious, even as ETF flows show demand is not waiting for perfect clarity.

items.title: Coldcard Flaw Continues Fueling Self-Custody Concerns
items.summary: The ongoing fallout from a multi-year firmware entropy bug in Coldcard hardware wallets, which enabled thieves to drain over 100 million dollars across waves of attacks, remains a hot topic. Users rushed to move funds and some confidence in pure self-custody took a hit, correlating with heavier ETF inflows as capital sought perceived safer institutional wrappers. Traders care because it highlights operational risks that can drive short-term flows into ETFs and exchanges while underscoring the need for rigorous key management.
items.impact: Boosts ETF demand amid lingering confidence hit

items.title: US July Jobs Report Shocks with 23k Loss
items.summary: The July nonfarm payrolls came in at a decline of 23,000 jobs, far below the roughly 80,000 gain expected, with prior months revised sharply lower. Unemployment edged to 4.1 percent mainly because people left the labor force, and wage growth slowed to 3.2 percent year-over-year. This soft print has cut the odds of a September Fed rate hike and highlights labor market risks alongside sticky inflation. Crypto traders should watch closely as it reduces near-term tightening pressure and supports risk assets.
items.impact: Lowers rate-hike odds, supportive for Bitcoin and risk assets

items.title: Yields Drop and Dollar Softens on Soft Payrolls
items.summary: Ten-year Treasury yields fell to around 4.65 percent and the US dollar index eased after the weak jobs data scaled back Fed hike expectations. Stocks rallied with the S&P 500 hitting a record as markets priced a more patient central bank. Front-end yields dropped more sharply, reflecting lower odds of September action. For crypto traders this easing in financial conditions is typically a positive backdrop unless inflation data flips the script next week.
items.impact: Easier financial conditions lift risk appetite

items.title: Trump Revives Push to Fire Fed's Lisa Cook
items.summary: The White House sent Fed Governor Lisa Cook a letter stating it is considering her removal over unproven mortgage fraud allegations and gave her 21 days to respond. This follows a Supreme Court setback earlier this year that kept her in place. The move reignites debates over Federal Reserve independence under Chair Kevin Warsh. Traders should note potential volatility or perceptions of political pressure that could influence policy expectations and market confidence in the central bank.
items.impact: Adds uncertainty around Fed independence and policy path

items.title: Weak Jobs Complicate Fed Inflation Fight
items.summary: Weekend analysis highlights how the soft July payrolls create a tougher balancing act for Chair Warsh, with a cooling labor market colliding against still-elevated inflation. Some officials had been leaning hawkish, but the data buys time and may favor patience into the September meeting. Bond markets had been doing some of the tightening work via higher yields, which eased after the print. Crypto traders care because it keeps the door open for a prolonged pause rather than immediate hikes.
items.impact: Increases odds of Fed pause, data-dependent path ahead

items.title: Focus Shifts to July CPI Release Wednesday
items.summary: With no major US data due this Sunday, markets are already positioning for the July Consumer Price Index on August 12, followed by PPI. The weak jobs report makes the inflation numbers even more pivotal for whether the Fed can stay on hold or feels forced to hike. Consensus eyes modest monthly gains but sticky year-over-year readings remain a risk amid earlier energy pressures. Traders should prepare for volatility as this will heavily shape September FOMC odds and risk asset direction.
items.impact: Key catalyst for near-term Fed pricing and market moves

items.title: Fed Hike Odds Fall Sharply After Jobs Miss
items.summary: Futures markets slashed the probability of a September rate increase to the low-to-mid 40 percent range from over 50 percent before the report, with year-end hike expectations also trimmed. Several Fed voices had recently argued for tighter policy to tackle inflation still above target. The data shift gives doves more ammunition while keeping the path highly dependent on incoming prices. For Bitcoin this reduces an immediate headwind from higher rates.
items.impact: Reduced tightening premium supports crypto and equities

items.title: Iran Demands US Concessions Before Reopening Hormuz
items.summary: Iran says a deal with Oman on new shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz is in the final stages, but the waterway stays closed until the US meets sweeping demands. Those include lifting the naval blockade and sanctions, paying reparations, ending military action, and withdrawing forces. Another ADNOC vessel was hit by a missile in the strait. Traders should care because this chokepoint handles about a fifth of global oil and LNG; delayed reopening keeps energy prices elevated and supports a risk-off tone across markets including crypto.
items.impact: Prolongs oil supply shock and inflation pressure, weighing on risk assets

items.title: Houthis Strike Saudi Aramco Jazan Refinery
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis claimed a drone attack on Saudi Aramco's Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast, sparking a fire that was later extinguished with no injuries reported. The strike came days after Saudi Arabia signed a mutual defense pact with Turkey and Pakistan and follows earlier Houthi hits that previously forced a temporary shutdown. This expands the energy war beyond Hormuz into another critical oil infrastructure and shipping zone, raising the odds of further supply disruptions that keep oil supported and risk appetite suppressed.
items.impact: Heightens Middle East energy risk premium and volatility

items.title: Netanyahu Rejects Trump's 15-Point Gaza Plan
items.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel rejects President Trump's Board of Peace 15-point plan for Gaza and will not withdraw forces until Hamas is fully disarmed. The rejection comes amid continued fighting and complicates US-brokered efforts to move the conflict into a longer-term stabilization phase. For traders this keeps a major regional flashpoint unresolved, sustaining geopolitical risk premium that can spill into oil, safe-havens, and broader risk assets.
items.impact: Extends Middle East uncertainty and risk-off pressure

items.title: Saudi, Turkey, Pakistan Sign Mutual Defense Pact
items.summary: Leaders of Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, pledging that an attack on one will be treated as an attack on all, similar to a NATO-style clause. The pact was struck amid the ongoing Iran conflict and Houthi threats, as Gulf states seek extra security guarantees. Markets will watch whether this new Sunni alignment deters further escalation or draws more players into regional fights, with knock-on effects for energy security and alliance dynamics.
items.impact: New alliance could stabilize or further polarize the region

items.title: US Senate Passes Sweeping Russia Energy Sanctions Bill
items.summary: The US Senate voted 86-11 to pass the Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, targeting Russian energy revenues, officials, financial institutions and the shadow fleet while authorizing tariffs of up to 100 percent on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The bill now heads to the House. If enacted it could squeeze Russian export flows, force buyers like China and India to adjust, and add another layer of trade and energy market friction that markets will price as growth and inflation risk.
items.impact: Potential new tariffs and energy disruptions hit global growth outlook

items.title: Ukraine and Russia Exchange Drone Strikes on Energy and Cities
items.summary: Russian authorities reported five killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Belgorod, while Ukraine said Russian strikes damaged Odesa port infrastructure and fuel facilities. Both sides continue targeting energy and logistics sites. Persistent Black Sea and energy infrastructure attacks keep grain and fuel export risks alive and remind markets that the war remains a chronic source of commodity and risk-asset volatility with no near-term resolution in sight.
items.impact: Sustains background geopolitical and commodity volatility
